mappings.note: Five sub-parts that between them cover the definition of corrosion, rusting, tarnishing, why corrosion matters and how to prevent it - LO-7 end to end, and the single best-fitting item in the chapter for that outcome.

Four of five sub-parts are extraction stages (concentration, roasting, roasting-only for mercury, electrolytic reduction), so LO-6 leads; sub-part (i) on top-of-series metals not occurring free needs the ranking, hence LO-2. Note sub-part (ii) is froth flotation, which sits beyond the class-10 core.
Defines the ionic bond, explains its formation and builds magnesium chloride. Entirely bond formation, which C 1.1 names at competency level and no learning outcome in this frame covers.

Sub-parts (i)-(iii) are electrolytic refining (LO-6). Sub-part (iv) sets two beakers of the same copper sulphate solution differing only in the metal strip dipped, over the same two hours - a controlled two-metal reactivity comparison (C 8.2-LO-2), whose explanation needs the zinc/copper/silver ranking (LO-2).

A results grid from parallel trials of four metals against four salt solutions; the student must infer the order and then choose a safe storage container. LO-2 for the ordering, C 8.2-LO-2 because the reasoning is over controlled experimental data rather than a recalled series.
Identifies sodium from a property profile - vigorous reaction with water, basic solution, pop test, low melting point. One metal, its own properties, so LO-1 and not the series.
Electrolyte, electrode half-reactions, anode mud and which metals are refined this way - all the refining stage of LO-6.

The passage is the reactivity series and most sub-parts read off it (LO-2), but one asks for the extraction method for the most reactive metals, which is LO-6. Two codes because the item deliberately crosses from ranking to extraction.

Mineral versus ore, native occurrence and named sulphide and halide ores - the occurrence front end of LO-6. DEFECT: sub-part (iii) is stored truncated as 'What is native of ...' with the key answering 'Horn silver (AgCl)', so the stem cannot be read as printed.

Every sub-part is a position judgement on the series - which metal copper can displace, which element sits above hydrogen, the most and the least reactive. LO-2 throughout, with no extraction or corrosion content.

Iron in copper sulphate is a displacement (LO-2), the copper ore and sodium extraction sub-parts are LO-6, and the very dilute nitric acid sub-part is the metal+acid exception (LO-1). DEFECT: the stored activity-series table ends 'Copper Silver Gold Mercury', placing mercury below gold; the correct order runs copper, mercury, silver, gold.

Sub-part (i) asks for a physical property that separates metals from non-metals (LO-1); the rest - bond type, formula of magnesium chloride and the shared valence shell of oxygen and sulphur - is bonding and configuration, which only the competency covers.
Named ores, extraction equations for copper, the definition of calcination and native metals - four stages of LO-6 in one case study.
Why carbon fails for sodium, the electrolysis steps, a carbon-reduction example and why the chloride must be molten rather than aqueous. All of it is LO-6, which bands metals by reactivity itself.

Thermite reduction as an extraction route (LO-6), with the choice of aluminium as reducing agent resting on it outranking manganese and iron (LO-2). The oxidised/reduced sub-part is redox vocabulary that no outcome in this frame covers.

Rust's formula and name, galvanisation, the definition of an alloy and two copper alloys. LO-7 is the one outcome that names both galvanisation and alloying, so this case study fits it better than any other item in the alloy family.

POOR FIT. The passage and both answered sub-parts are about the octet rule and noble-gas configurations, with no metal or non-metal anywhere in the demand. Competency cited as least wrong. DEFECT: only two sub-parts are keyed although the item is stored as a four-mark case study.

Parallel trials of four metals against four salt solutions, tabulated; the student ranks them and then predicts a further observation. Same basis as the other results-table case study: LO-2 for the ranking, C 8.2-LO-2 because the evidence is controlled experimental data.
